theory.intro: The **velocity** of a particle is the rate of change of its displacement with time. If the displacement is $x(t)$, differentiate to find the velocity $v = \dot{x} = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.
facts: Common units of velocity are metres per second, $\text{m/s}$, or kilometres per hour, $\text{km/h}$.
**Initial velocity** is the velocity at time $t = 0$, that is $v(0) = \dot{x}(0)$.
A particle is **at rest** (or **stationary**) when its velocity is zero: $v(t) = 0$.
To find the position when at rest, solve $v(t) = 0$ for $t$, then substitute that time into $x(t)$.
The particle moves in the **positive direction** (right/up) when $v(t) > 0$, and the **negative direction** (left/down) when $v(t) < 0$.
To find the velocity at the origin, solve $x(t) = 0$ for the time(s), then substitute into $v(t)$.
steps: Differentiate the displacement function $x(t)$ with respect to $t$ using differentiation rules to find $v(t) = \dot{x}$.
To find initial velocity, substitute $t = 0$ into $v(t)$.
To find velocity at time $t = c$, substitute $t = c$ into $v(t)$.
To find when the particle is at rest, set $v(t) = 0$ and solve for $t \ge 0$.
To find position when at rest, evaluate $x(t)$ at the stationary time.

foundation.question_text: The displacement of a particle moving along a line is $x = 3t^2 - 12t + 5$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Find the formula for the velocity $v(t) = \dot{x}$.
A particle moves with displacement $x(t) = t^3 - 4t^2 + 7$ metres. Find its initial velocity and its velocity at $t = 3\text{ s}$.
A particle has displacement $x = 2t^2 - 8t + 3$ metres. Find the time when the particle is instantaneously at rest, and determine its displacement at this instant.
The vertical displacement of a launched object is $x = 40t - 5t^2$ metres. Find the velocity function $\dot{x}$.
A model vehicle moves along a track with displacement $x = 10 + 6t - t^2$ centimetres for $t \ge 0$. Find the vehicle's velocity after $4\text{ seconds}$.
A particle moves according to $x = t^2 - 5t + 6$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Find the times when it passes through the origin, and calculate its velocity at each of these times.
A projectile has height $h = 30t - 5t^2$ metres above the ground. Find the time taken to reach its maximum height where its velocity is zero.

development.question_text: A particle moves with displacement $x = t^3 - 9t$ metres for $t \ge 0$. Find the velocity of the particle when it returns to the origin ($x = 0, t > 0$).
The displacement of a particle is given by $x = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 24t + 10$ metres. Find the two times when the particle is instantaneously at rest.
Two particles $A$ and $B$ have displacements $x_A = t^2 + 3t$ and $x_B = 11t - 5$ metres respectively. Find the time $t$ when both particles have the same velocity.
A particle moves with displacement $x = \dfrac{1}{3}t^3 - 2t^2 + 3t - 4$ metres. Find the time interval during which the particle is moving in the negative direction ($v < 0$).
A particle moves such that $x = t^2 - 6t + 8$ metres. Find the velocity of the particle when its displacement is $x = 3\text{ m}$ for the first time.
A particle moves with displacement $x = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2$ metres. Find its displacement at the instant it comes to rest for the second time.
A sounding rocket's altitude is $y = 80t - 5t^2$ metres. Find its velocity after $2\text{ s}$ and after $10\text{ s}$, and interpret the difference in the signs of the velocity.
development.solution_text:
$v(t) = 80 - 10t$
$\text{At } t = 2: v(2) = 80 - 20 = +60\text{ m/s (ascending)}$
$\text{At } t = 10: v(10) = 80 - 100 = -20\text{ m/s (descending)}$

mastery.question_text: A particle's displacement is $x(t) = 2t^3 - 9t^2 + 12t - 4$ metres. Find all times when the particle is at rest, and calculate the distance between these two stationary positions.
A particle moves according to $x = t^3 - 7t^2 + 10t$ metres. Find all times when the particle is at the origin, and evaluate its velocity at each of these times.

Two particles $P$ and $Q$ move on the same line with displacements $x_P = t^2 + 4t$ and $x_Q = 2t^3 - 3t^2 - 8t + 1$ metres. Find the positive time $t$ when particle $Q$ has twice the velocity of particle $P$.
